outline.title: Relay gain adapts to stimulus history in a synthetic preparation
Abstract
outline.claim: We study how a relay stage adjusts its gain when the same stimulus is repeated.

outline.title: 1 Introduction
outline.claim: Adaptation is widely observed, yet the stage at which gain changes remains unclear.

outline.title: 2 Methods
outline.claim: Stimuli of 200 ms were delivered at 1 Hz for ten trials.

outline.title: 3 Results
outline.claim: The first trial produced the largest response and later trials declined.

outline.title: 4 Discussion
outline.claim: The gain change is already visible at the relay, which places the adaptation before the recorder.

outline.title: 5 Conclusion
outline.claim: Relay gain declines with repeated stimulation and the decline is intrinsic to the relay.
